stages.reference: Create a close material reference for black stained glass made in an austere, centuries-old workshop. Its appearance is deep smoke-charcoal, but it remains glass rather than polished stone: thin passages admit muted gray light while thicker regions build subtle optical depth. Hand coloring leaves a faint difference in pigment density, and cooling produces almost invisible waviness. Weather has softened the surface with a trace of mineral haze, not coated it in dirt. Keep reflections weak and diffuse; the strength of the material comes from its calm darkness and controlled translucency. Avoid obsidian facets, metallic shine, black plastic, dramatic cracks, window frames, etched decoration or an opaque painted square. Its paired detail layer should be almost imperceptible against the same black glass.
